summary: Deprecates the use of MD5 and SHA-1 hashes in digital signatures in TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2, because those algorithms are increasingly vulnerable to attack. It does not deprecate SHA-1 when used within HMAC for record protection. The document updates RFC 5246.

eli5.summary: Some old stamps are now easy to forge. This note tells computers to stop trusting those two stamp types for signatures.

subtitle: TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2 may no longer use MD5 or SHA-1 in digital signatures.

tldr.problem: TLS 1.2 allowed MD5 and SHA-1 for signature hashing, but both are subject to collision attacks.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9155 updates RFC 5246 so clients and servers MUST NOT use MD5 or SHA-1 in signature algorithm lists, key exchange and certificate verification messages, and IANA marks SHA-1 schemes as not recommended.
tldr.outcome: MD5 and SHA-1 MUST NOT be used for digital signatures in (D)TLS 1.2, while SHA-1 with HMAC for record protection is not deprecated.

today: RFC 9155 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5246. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why MD5 and SHA-1 Were Retired
sections.content:
RFC 5246 specifies MD5 and SHA-1 for signature hashing in (D)TLS 1.2. Both have been shown to be insecure and subject to collision attacks. The RFC cites NIST deprecating SHA-1 in 2011 and disallowing it for digital signatures at the end of 2013, and a 2017 result showing that SHA-1 collision attacks are practical.

The CA/Browser Forum has also deprecated SHA-1 for certificate signatures. RFC 9155 updates RFC 5246 so MD5 and SHA-1 MUST NOT be used for digital signatures. SHA-1 with HMAC, as used in record protection, is not deprecated.
sections.eli5: Two old secret-stamp designs can now be faked, so they should no longer be used to prove who signed something.

sections.title: The Rules for Each Message
sections.content:
Each handshake message gets its own rule.

  • signature_algorithms extension: clients MUST include it and MUST NOT include MD5 and SHA-1 in it.
  • CertificateRequest: servers SHOULD NOT include MD5 and SHA-1.
  • ServerKeyExchange: servers MUST NOT include them. A client that sees one MUST abort the connection with an illegal_parameter alert.
  • CertificateVerify: clients MUST NOT include them. A server that receives one MUST abort with an illegal_parameter alert.
sections.eli5: At every step of the greeting, neither side may offer the old stamps, and if one shows up anyway, the other side hangs up.

sections.title: IANA Registry Updates
sections.content:
IANA changed the recommended status of SHA-1-based schemes in the "TLS SignatureScheme" registry to "N" (not recommended), as defined by RFC 8447. The entries are 0x0201 (rsa_pkcs1_sha1) and 0x0203 (ecdsa_sha1).

IANA also updated the reference for the "TLS SignatureAlgorithm" and "TLS HashAlgorithm" registries to include this document.
sections.eli5: The official list now marks the two SHA-1 entries with a warning label.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The concern is that (D)TLS 1.2 implementations might fall back to SHA-1. The document deprecates MD5 and SHA-1 for digital signatures to address that, while leaving SHA-1 with HMAC for record protection alone.
sections.eli5: The worry is that computers quietly slip back to the old stamp, so the rule says not to.
